title: Pauline Theology
description: Paul's letters in an order that builds conceptually rather than canonically: the gospel defended, the church pastored, the system laid out in Romans, then the prison letters' cosmic vision and the pastoral handoff.
audience: A reader ready to work through Paul seriously, one letter building on the last.

sequence.note: Start with Paul's (likely) earliest letter: the gospel's basics and the blessed hope.
The immediate correction — eschatology gone wrong and how Paul steadies it.
The gospel defined by fire: faith versus works of the law, freedom versus slavery.
Now the gospel pastoring a messy church: the cross against factions.
Gifts, the body, and the love chapter.
The resurrection chapter — Paul's gospel 'of first importance.'
What apostolic ministry actually costs: treasure in clay jars.
Now the full system, argued from the ground up.
Union with Christ, the Spirit, no condemnation, no separation.
Election, Israel, and mercy on all — Paul's hardest and deepest stretch.
From prison, the cosmic Christ over every power.
Colossians' theology applied to one household and one runaway slave.
The church in God's eternal plan.
The Christ-hymn and joy from a prison cell.
The handoff begins: ordering God's household.
Paul's last words: 'I have finished the race.'
